First public release of **OpenCVEC**, a self-hosted CVE checker that proves exposure on assets you own, using canaries instead of exploitation.

## Highlights

- **Proof by canary.** Each check makes the target resolve a single-use DNS name bound by HMAC to one asset and one check, call the HTTP receiver, or read back a **canary file** planted on the asset. Built-in authoritative DNS server and HTTP receiver.
- **Anti-abuse by design.**
  - Mandatory proof of ownership (DNS TXT, /.well-known or administrator allowlist), re-validated before every campaign.
  - Fixed payloads; the network guard blocks DNS rebinding and access to private or metadata addresses.
  - Rate limits and an append-only, hash-chained audit log.
- **Signed YAML plugins.** Every checker is a plugin. 10 official plugins are embedded and preinstalled, including offline:
  - DNS callback: Log4Shell, Text4Shell, Spring Cloud Function, Confluence OGNL, PHP-CGI;
  - canary file: Apache traversal;
  - fingerprint: regreSSHion, PHP2Shell, WP2Shell, FortiBleed exposure.

  New plugins are installed from the official catalog or by file, after review and Ed25519 signature check (`opencvec plugin keygen | lint | sign | verify | index`).
- **Honeytoken alerts.** A canary file read outside a check raises a compromise alert.
- **Operations.** Notifications (webhook JSON / Slack / Teams, SMTP), scheduled checks, personal API tokens, PDF / HTML / JSON reports with SHA-256 fingerprints, data retention, English and French interface.
- **Small footprint.** A 7 MB distroless image for amd64 and arm64, about 11 MiB of RAM at idle, plus PostgreSQL. Two deployment modes:
  - internal network, through a conditional DNS forwarder;
  - Internet, through NS delegation.

## Validation

12 lab scenarios against real vulnerable and patched targets (`lab/compose.yaml`, `scripts/lab-e2e.sh`, `scripts/lab-plugins-e2e.sh`). Go unit and PostgreSQL integration tests, front-end tests, `govulncheck` and `npm audit` clean.

## Known limitations

- Not yet tested on a real public DNS delegation or a real corporate DNS forwarder.
- Confluence, PHP-CGI and FortiBleed plugins are covered by unit tests only (no free lab image).
- Server-generated texts (verdict summaries, errors) and plugin descriptions are in French.

## Install

```sh
docker pull ghcr.io/eizi0/opencvec:v0.1.0
```

See [README](https://github.com/Eizi0/OpenCVEC#installation) and [docs/deployment.md](https://github.com/Eizi0/OpenCVEC/blob/main/docs/deployment.md).
